stem: Which early management step is most appropriate for a child with diabetic ketoacidosis after the initial ABC assessment?

options.text: Insert two IV lines, commence rehydration fluids, and take bloods
Wait for urine ketones before obtaining IV access
Start subcutaneous insulin and discharge with clinic review
Begin oral fluids and a regular diet
Prioritise thyroid testing before circulation management

explanation: Insert two IV lines, commence rehydration fluids, and take bloods is the correct early management approach after ABC assessment in diabetic ketoacidosis.

citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because early DKA management includes establishing IV access, starting rehydration fluids, and taking bloods promptly.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because urine ketones should not delay immediate IV access and blood sampling in suspected DKA.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because subcutaneous insulin and discharge are not appropriate initial management for DKA.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because oral fluids and a regular diet are not appropriate during initial DKA resuscitation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because thyroid testing is not the immediate priority before circulation management in DKA.
